subtitle.text: Danny: I hope it’s clay today.
Brad: You always hope it’s clay.
Danny: Modeling clay is the best!
Tina: I wish it were gym class.
Mr. Smith: Children, please. Please sit down.
Danny: I hope it’s clay.
Please, I hope it’s clay.
Mr. Smith: Today, for art class we will be using . . .
Danny: CLAY?
Mr. Smith: Yes, Danny, we’re using clay.
Not so loud next time.
Danny: Sorry.
Brad: You’re always so excited!
Danny: Shh. I don’t want to get into more trouble!
Mr. Smith: Here you go, Tina.
Tina: I just want black and white
please. Mr. Smith: Why is that,
Tina? Tina: Well, those are the colors of a soccer
ball. Brad: Actually, black isn’t really a
color. Mr. Smith: Very good,
Brad. Black is really no color at
all. Danny: How did you know
that? Brad: My computer has all the
answers. Mr. Smith: Children, I’m handing out seven colors because . .
. Danny: Who’s this guy
Roy? Mr. Smith: Well, if you’d let me explain . .
. Danny: Is he a new kid in
class? Mr. Smith: No, Danny, Roy G. Biv is . .
. A cloud. It must have been a
cloud. Danny: Who is Roy G.
Biv? Mr. Smith: Yes. That’s what I was
saying. Roy G. Biv stands for . .
. Tina: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue . .
. Brad: I knew
that. Mr. Smith: Very good, Tina. Keep
going. Tina: Well, those are the colors in front of
me. Mr. Smith: Brad, do you know the
rest? Brad: Indigo and
violet. The colors of the
rainbow. Mr. Smith: Very good,
Brad! Danny: Can we
start? My imagination is
going crazy!! Mr. Smith: Danny, it’s not nice
to interrupt. Class, you may now begin.
Create whatever you want.
Tina: What are you doing?
Danny: I’m just looking.
Tina: At what?
Danny: What are you making?
Is it a tree?
Tina: It’s going to be a soccer player.
Danny: That gives me an idea!
Brad: How’s it going over there, Mr. Artist?
Danny: I don’t think I’ve got it right yet.
Mr. Smith: Danny, more art and less talk.
Danny: But when I talk, it helps my hands move!
Mr. Smith: Danny, don’t bother the other students.
Tina: You’re going to get into trouble.
Danny: I need to look at you more closely.
Tina: What are you talking about?
Danny: Come here and look! See?
Tina: That’s pretty good, Danny.
Danny: Yeah, but I’m missing something.
Brad: She’s right. That looks good, Danny.
Dave: Hey! Look at this!
Chuck: Well, well, well. Isn’t this cute!
Danny: Just leave me alone.
Chuck: Aww. He likes the girl!
Dave: He’s in love with her.
Chuck: Are you guys going to get married?
Danny: Give me that!
Dave: He wants his girlfriend back.
Danny: She’s not my girlfriend!
Stop! You’re squishing my model!
Tina: Why don’t you leave him alone?
Chuck: Isn’t that sweet?
She's standing up for her boyfriend.
Tina: You don’t want to make me angry.
Dave: Why? What’s going to happen?
Tina: Have you forgotten what happened last week?
Chuck: Here’s your little doll back!
Dave: You’re lucky that your girlfriend is strong.
Danny: SHE’S NOT MY GIRLFRIEND!
Tina: Danny, quiet.
Mr. Smith: What’s going on here?
Why are you yelling, Danny?
Danny: These guys are driving me crazy!
Mr. Smith: Danny, I think you’re driving me crazy.
Tina: No, really, Mr. Smith.
These boys were picking on Danny.
Mr. Smith: Is that true, boys?
Dave: No, Mr. Smith.
Chuck: We just like his clay models.
Dave: Yeah. We think they’re really good.
Mr. Smith: Danny? What do you have to say?
Danny: They . . . are . . . big . . . stinking . . . LIARS!
Mr. Smith: Danny, that’s enough!
Tina: Danny, calm down.
Brad: Mr. Smith?
Mr. Smith: Yes, Brad.
Brad: I can prove that Danny is innocent.
Mr. Smith: Brad, please return to your desk.
Everybody, back to your desks.
Danny: But Mr. Smith. . .
Mr. Smith: That’s enough, Danny.
We will not be using clay anymore today!
Mr. Smith: Please pull out your workbooks.
Tina: Sorry, Danny.
Dave: We’ll see you at recess, Danny.
Danny: No more clay?
Mr. Smith: Now, Danny . . .
Danny: Yes, Mr. Smith?
Mr. Smith: You can’t yell in
class. Danny: But they were being mean to
me! Mr. Smith: Danny . .
. Danny: They’re
bullies! Mr. Smith: You were the one making all the
noise. Danny: I’m just an excited
guy! Mr. Smith: Danny, please throw out your
clay. Danny: I don’t want
to. Mr. Smith: Please do it
now. Thank you. Now, go sit in the corner until recess. Danny:
Please! I promise to be quiet!
Mr. Smith: No. You’ll sit there and think about what you’ve done.
Danny: Do I have to?
Mr. Smith: Yes, Danny. You do.
Brad: I thought your models looked good, Danny.
Danny: Thanks. They’re garbage now.
Tina: You tried to stand up to those bullies.
Good for you.
Danny: But now I’m in trouble.
Dave: Ha-ha!
Chuck: Ha-ha!
Danny: It’s not fair.
Mr. Smith: Now, Danny, I want you to put your head on the
desk. And think about what you
did. Danny: I was making great art, but . .
. Mr. Smith: What’s the lesson,
Danny? Danny: I don’t
know. Mr. Smith: You shouldn’t get so excited in the
future. Danny: I’ve got a great
imagination! I can’t help
it! Mr. Smith: Okay, class. Turn to page six in your
books. Chuck: Hey, Danny. I’ll save that little doll you
made. Danny: Leave
me alone. Chuck: Then you can have
it forever. Danny: Dumb people are always getting me into trouble .
. . I just wanted to play with my clay. That’s
all. Who’s that?
Danny: Who are you?
Hopian: It’s all
right. There’s nothing to be afraid
of. Danny: What are you doing
here? Hopian: My name is
Hopian, Danny. Danny: How do you know
my name? Hopian: I’ve been
watching you. Danny:
Watching me? Why? Hopian: Only you can
help us, Danny. I
come from Ginormous. It’s a land filled with
giants like myself. The people of Ginormous were
usually very happy. We all got along with
each other. We knew how
to play. Families used to gather for picnics in the
colorful gardens. The giant children used to sing and
paint pictures. My son used to make clay
castles. Danny: Sounds like fun!
What happened? Hopian: Our color is
disappearing, Danny. Danny: What do
you mean? Hopian: I noticed it about
a month ago.I went outside one day to get ready for
a party. Our friends and neighbors were going to join
us. I looked around the garden, and then I noticed
something. I walked up to a plant that was normally bright
blue. But now it was gray!
I bent down to look at the
grass. I noticed that it had faded too.
I was surprised, and started to feel sad.
Danny: That’s terrible!
Hopian: As the weeks passed, I noticed more and more
gray. My friends were no longer very happy.
People seemed to
change.Something evil is happening to my world. My
people are very sad. They miss
color. That’s
why I came to you. Danny:
Why me? Hopian:
Everyone in Ginormous is forgetting all about color.
But you still have a colorful imagination. Danny:
But what can I do?
I’m just a little kid.
Hopian: I brought something for you, Danny.
It came from my
world. Danny: That’s so
cool! Hopian: It’s beautiful, isn’t
it? Danny: But I thought all the color was gone from
your world! Hopian: So
did I. But I found something the
other day. I have a young son
named Bello. He is two
years old. When I came home the other day, he
looked happy. He was running around with a big
smile. I guessed something was going on.
He led me into his
room. He took some clay from under his bed.
He started making a circus with it.
There were big blue horses, a large red tent, and a funny yellow clown. Bello
laughed. His eyes were shining. Then
I noticed something. His
beautiful fur was shining with color! I realized
that Bello’s imagination was giving him color. I was
so happy that I cried. I took his
clay into my hands and closed my eyes. I wondered how
this little bit of clay could help. When I opened
my eyes, I was outside your classroom. Danny: The clay led
you to me? Hopian: My imagination led
me to you. Your ability with
clay will heal our world. It will be
a colorful, happy place again. Danny: I don’t
know how to do that! Hopian: I know
you can do it, Danny. Danny: But
you haven’t told me how! Hopian: Danny,
I can’t stay here any longer. I have
to go now. But
I’m going to leave this clay with you. Look for
it in your desk. Danny: Hopian,
don’t go! Hopian:
Danny, use your imagination. Find
your way to Ginormous. Once
you’re there, I’ll help you any way I can. Danny:
But I have no idea where Ginormous is! How
can I get there?
Hopian: Remember, your imagination can unlock any door.
Good-bye, Danny. I
know I’ll see you soon. Danny:
Hopian!
Hopian: Your imagination can unlock any . . .
Brad: It’s recess time.
Tina: Is everything okay?
Brad: Yeah, you were making strange noises.
We saw you moving like a jumping bean. Danny:
You didn’t see him? Tina
& Brad: See who? Danny:
Well, I saw him and I know he’s real!
Brad: Who’s real?
Danny: Aha! It’s here!
He left the clay for me.
Tina: Danny, you’re acting really weird.
Danny: Let’s go! Follow me to our secret place! Hurry!
You guys have to listen to me. Tina:
Okay. Danny:
And believe me. Brad:
Well, that depends on what you say. Danny:
Okay. I just had a visit. Brad:
You were asleep at your desk. Danny:
No, no. Just listen─
Brad: Well, you’re not making any sense.
Tina: Brad, just listen to Danny.
Danny: Thank you. My visitor was a giant named Hopian.
We have to go to his world. It’s
called Ginormous. We
have to bring back the lost color to his world. Tina: That’s
a good one, Danny! Brad: And
you were so serious the whole time! Tina: A
giant! Brad: Bring
back the lost color! Danny: I’m
serious! Brad:
Danny, you had a dream about art class. That’s all. Tina:
You have got the wildest imagination. Danny:
That’s what Hopian said! Tina:
Sorry, Danny. But I’d rather play soccer than listen to this. Danny:
No, I’ve got proof. Hopian
gave me something. Brad:

No. I wish it was a map, though. Here. Brad:
What’s that? Danny:
It’s clay from Hopian’s world. It’s
going to help us get there.
Brad: That’s just the clay from art class.
Tina: This clay is glowing, Brad.
That clay didn’t glow.
Danny: What is it?
Brad: This clay is not from our world.

I checked the Internet.

I told you I was telling the truth! Tina:
So this clay was given to you . . . by a giant? Danny:

Your imagination? Danny:

ALA KAZAAM KABLAM , TAKE ME TO GINORMOUS!

late. Danny: Just one

Wow. Brad: I knew that cloud looked

Danny: Hello? Hopian?
This isn’t how I pictured Ginormous.
Maybe we came to the wrong place. Brad:
I think we should go back and try again.
Tina: I don’t think we’re going anywhere, guys.
Danny: Why not?
Tina: Because the door has disappeared!
Brad: But the door was right there!
Tina: I know where it was.
Danny: How is that possible?
Brad: We’re doomed!
Tina: Now, let’s not get scared.
Danny: Why not?
Tina: Because if there’s a way in, there’s got to be a way out.
Brad: Let me ask my computer!
Danny: Well?
Brad: I asked it, "What’s the best way to get out?"
Danny: And what did it say?
Brad: It said, "Find an exit."
Danny: That computer is useless!
Tina: Danny, calm down.
Brad: She’s right. Getting upset won’t help.
Danny: Well, being calm isn’t helping.
Tina: It’s as if we’re in the woods.

Danny: I can make a compass!
Tina: What?

Brad: What good does that do?
Danny: Well . . .
Tina: If we keep walking in one direction, I’m sure we’ll find something.
Danny: She’s right. Standing here won’t help.
Brad: Something feels funny.
Danny: Yeah, the ground is all squishy.
Tina: My shoes are getting wet.
Brad: Yeah. Mine too.
Tina: The ground is getting squishier!
Brad: Our feet are sinking in.
Danny: Whoa!
Brad: You must have stepped on a geyser!
Tina: Look at that!
Danny: Our footsteps are making puddles.
Brad: This isn’t good!
Tina: Let’s start running!
Danny: I can’t get my feet out!
Brad: This is really bad!
Tina: I wish I were a giant so I could just leap out of this.
Brad: If you were a giant, you’d just sink faster.
Danny: What are we going to do?
Tina: Look! Over there! We’re saved!
Danny: How are we saved?
Tina: We just need to get over there, to higher ground.
Brad: I wish your friend Hopian was here.
He could tell us what to do!
Danny: Ha-ha!
Brad: What are you so happy about?

Brad: What was it?
Danny: Imagination is the key,
remember? Tina: So, how do we imagine our way over to the
trees? Danny: I guess. .
. Brad: I’ve got
it! Think light
thoughts! Danny: What do you
mean? Brad: Think of the lightest thing you
can. Imagine that you're a feather or something.
Tina: It might work.
Brad: Let me test it out.
Tina: It’s working!
Brad: I made it! I made it!
We’re going to be safe.
Danny: What did you think of?
Brad: Marshmallows! I imagined that my feet were marshmallows!
Danny: Now I’m hungry.
Tina: It’s my turn!
Brad: Good job! Keep going!
Tina: That was easy.
Great idea, Brad!
It really works.
Brad: Come on, Danny. Your turn.
Danny: This’ll be easy!
Tina: He’ll be here in no
time! You’re really smart,
Brad. Brad: Yeah. I didn’t even need my computer this
time. Tina: Oh
no! Brad: Danny! What’s
happening? Danny: I was thinking of a
balloon. Then I started to think of a baboon instead!
Brad: Concentrate on the balloon!
Danny: I’m trying!
Brad: Let’s help him.
Brad & Tina: Balloon, balloon, balloon, balloon. . .
Good job, Danny!
Brad: Okay, now that we’re safe up here, where do we go?
Tina: Maybe we can swim?
Brad: We can’t swim through soggy land.
Besides, where would we swim to?
Danny: Hey, maybe if we imagine the giants’ world, we will appear there!
Danny: Okay, imagine Ginormous on the count of
three. Ready? One, two, three!
Brad: I don’t think this is working.
Danny: You’re both imagining Ginormous, right?
Tina: Yes, a world full of giants playing.
Brad: A giant world without color.
Danny: I don’t think you guys are picturing it right.
Tina: How can we imagine a place we’ve never seen?
Danny: You’re right.
But how else are we going to get out of here!
Ow! Brad:
What was that? Danny:
That was the sound of my foot on that tree! Tina:
The tree made a funny sound when you kicked it.
Brad: Not funny, hollow.
Danny: But trees aren’t hollow.
Brad: This one is.
Tina: A hollow tree!
Danny: What is it made of?
Brad: It looks like some kind of aluminum, just like a can.
Tina: How is it growing then?
Brad: I don’t think this tree has any roots.
Danny: It’s definitely not a real tree.
It was put here, not planted.
Brad: There might be something interesting underneath it.
Danny: How can we get it up?
Tina: The ground is too wet to dig.
The holes just keep filling up with
water. Brad: Hey,
guys? Danny:
What? Brad: Danny, Tina. Come and stand in a circle around the
tree. Okay, hold on tight to the tree, and when I say go, everyone, walk to the right.
Ready? Go!
Danny: Brad! The tree is moving!
Brad: Just as I thought, the tree is screwed into the ground.
And it’s made of aluminum, so it 's pretty light.
I think we can lift it. Tina:
Way to go, Brad! Danny:
Let’s get this tree out of here! Brad:
What’s down there? Tina:
I don’t know, but it’s dark and wet.
Brad: More water is the last thing we need!
Danny: Well, I think it looks safe.
Tina: I wonder what would happen if we jumped in.
Brad: That’s my point.
We don’t know what might happen!
Danny: Hey! It feels smooth, just like a waterslide.
Tina: A waterslide! They are so much fun.
Brad: You’re both crazy.
You don’t know where it leads.
Danny: It has to lead somewhere.
I think we should try it.
Tina: I’ll go first! Ready?
Start right after me, Brad!
Danny: You better go, Brad.
We don’t want to lose her.
One, two, three! I’m right behind you! Tina:
Wheee! This is incredible! Brad:
I think I’m going to be sick.
Danny: This is more fun than being in class!
Brad: Whoo-hoo!
Danny: That’s the spirit, Brad.
Tina: It’s about time we had fun!
Danny: Which way do we go?
Tina: I don’t know!
Brad, what do you think?
Brad: How should I know?!
Danny: Somebody decide quickly!
Tina: This way!
Brad: What if we went the wrong way?
Tina: Then this won’t be much fun anymore.
Danny: We haven’t done too badly, so far.
Brad: Oh yeah? Well, just look ahead.
Al threel: Aaah!

Danny: I’ve got an idea!

Tina: This better work!
Brad: Oh no!

Danny: Both of you, start

Danny! Brad: Hey, I’m the smart
one. Danny: More blowing, less
talking! That’s it, I think we’ve stopped falling.
Brad: I . . . can’t . . . blow . . . anymore!

Tina: Everybody blow!
Danny: Hurry!
Brad: Oh no!
Brad: That was close.

Now what are we going to do?

Ginormous! What about getting home?
Danny: We can’t go home.
You promised to help.

Tina: Oh, Brad! We need to help the giants.

Sure, that would be terrible. But
why is it my problem? Danny:

I guess you’re right. Tina:
Brad is right about one thing, though.

. My computer is
